_note: Places every original collection unit that semester-1/curriculum.json does not already map to a topic. A topic id attaches the unit to that Semester 1 topic; 'background' = needed earlier knowledge; 'related' = plausibly Semester 1 but not named in the published course description (confirm with the lecturer's outline); 'beyond' = not in the published Semester 1 description. The build fails if any unit is unplaced.

background: Review material the Semester 1 topics rely on: domains, function families, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions.
related: Related methods — check your lecturer’s outline
Standard Calculus I methods that the published MA 101 description does not name explicitly (for example L’Hôpital’s rule and Newton’s method). Read them if your outline includes them.
beyond: Beyond Semester 1: integration and differential equations
Not in the published MA 101 description. Kept for later reference; you do not need these for Semester 1 unless your lecturer adds them.

background: How derivatives and accumulation connect to motion. Useful if your physics course uses calculus.
related: Related mechanics — check your lecturer’s outline
Mechanics topics often taught in a first physics course but not named in the published PHY 101 description.
beyond: Beyond Semester 1: rotation, gravitation, fluids, waves, heat, electricity and modern physics
Not in the published PHY 101 description (fundamentals, laws of motion and their applications, laboratory work and graphing). Kept for later courses.

background: Background: matter, measurement, formulas and moles
The quantitative foundation that reactions in solution, solutions and gases rely on: classification, measurement, unit conversion, formulas and the mole.
related: Related topics — check your lecturer’s outline
Topics connected to the published CHEM 101 list (intermolecular forces, phases, free energy) that may or may not be assessed in your section.
beyond: Beyond Semester 1: kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, nuclear, organic and coordination chemistry
Not in the published CHEM 101 description. Typically part of the following chemistry course.
